Department of Chemistry, University of Utah, Salt Lake City, UT

ACADEMIC APPOINTMENTS
University of Utah, Department of Chemistry · Assistant Professor · Aug 2025 – Present
California Institute of Technology, Division of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering · Postdoctoral Scholar · Sep 2023 – Jul 2025

EDUCATION
University of Wisconsin–Madison · Ph.D. Chemistry (Inorganic), 2023 · Dissertation on earth-abundant metal catalysts for C–H functionalization
Macalester College · B.A. Chemistry, summa cum laude, Phi Beta Kappa, 2018

RESEARCH
Group focus: first-row transition-metal catalysis for late-stage functionalization and mechanistic study by in situ spectroscopy. Group as of Fall 2026: 3 Ph.D. students, 2 undergraduates. Current projects: (1) nickel-catalyzed amination of unactivated C(sp3)–H bonds with ligand-controlled site selectivity; (2) operando X-ray absorption and EPR studies of first-row metal catalytic cycles; (3) earth-abundant metal photocatalysis for late-stage functionalization of drug-like molecules.

FUNDING
• National Science Foundation, CHE Division, Chemical Synthesis program · Principal Investigator · $540,000 · 2026–2029 · "Nickel-catalyzed C(sp3)–H amination guided by operando spectroscopy"
• University of Utah Research Incentive Seed Grant · PI · $50,000 · 2025–2026
• Start-up package, University of Utah · $1.1M · 2025
• ACS Petroleum Research Fund, Doctoral New Investigator grant · PI · $110,000 · 2026–2028

FELLOWSHIPS AND AWARDS
• NSF Graduate Research Fellowship, 2019–2022
• Wisconsin Alumni Research Foundation Dissertation Fellowship, 2022–2023
• ACS Division of Inorganic Chemistry Young Investigator Award (symposium speaker), 2023
• Macalester Chemistry Department Senior Prize, 2018

PUBLICATIONS (12; * corresponding author)
Citations: about 620 total (Google Scholar, September 2026); h-index 9.
Independent career
12. Two group members and [name]*. "Ligand-controlled site selectivity in nickel-catalyzed amination of unactivated C(sp3)–H bonds." J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2026, 148, 9120–9131.
11. One group member, two collaborators and [name]*. "Operando X-ray absorption study of a Ni(I)/Ni(III) amination cycle." Organometallics 2026, 45, 2210–2219.
Postdoctoral (Caltech)
10. Co-author (2nd of 6). "Photoinduced copper-catalyzed C–N coupling of secondary alkyl halides." J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147, 4410–4420.
9. Co-author (3rd of 5). "A general asymmetric alkylation of amides via copper photoredox catalysis." Nature Chem. 2025, 17, 612–619.
8. First author (of 4). "Mechanism of enantioselective C–N bond formation under copper photocatalysis." J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2024, 146, 18822–18833.
Graduate (Wisconsin)
7. First author (of 3). "Iron-catalyzed directed C–H borylation: scope and kinetic analysis." Angew. Chem. Int. Ed. 2023, 62, e202301122.
6. Co-author (2nd of 4). "Spectroscopic characterization of a high-spin iron(III) alkyl intermediate." Inorg. Chem. 2022, 61, 15002–15010.
5. First author (of 3). "Cobalt-catalyzed C–H alkenylation of benzamides with internal alkynes." J. Org. Chem. 2022, 87, 6611–6622.
4. Co-author (3rd of 4). "Redox-active ligands for base-metal C–H functionalization: a perspective." Chem. Sci. 2021, 12, 9900–9912.
3. First author (of 2). "A tridentate N,N,O ligand platform for iron-catalyzed C–H activation." Organometallics 2021, 40, 1877–1886.
2. Co-author (4th of 5). "Computational and experimental study of cobalt-mediated C–H cleavage." Dalton Trans. 2020, 49, 7701–7710.
Undergraduate (Macalester)
1. Co-author (2nd of 3). "Synthesis of pyridyl-pyrazolate copper complexes." Inorg. Chim. Acta 2018, 471, 450–456.

• Teaching Assistant, General Chemistry and Inorganic Laboratory, Wisconsin, 2018–2019

SERVICE
